question: Which statement links all three levels of description correctly?
correct: Limewater turns cloudy (macroscopic) because Ca²⁺ and CO₃²⁻ ions form insoluble calcium carbonate (particulate), Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O (symbolic)
before: Limewater turns cloudy because it is cold
after: Limewater turns cloudy (particulate) because CO₂ molecules dissolve in the water (macroscopic), shown by the formula CaCO₃ alone (symbolic)
Limewater turns cloudy (symbolic) because calcium carbonate is a white solid (macroscopic), and Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O shows the ions (particulate)

question: Why is sodium chloride safe to eat when sodium and chlorine are both dangerous?
correct: In the compound, sodium and chloride are ions held in a lattice and no longer have the reactivity of the free elements
before: It contains only a little sodium
after: Sodium and chlorine stay as free atoms in the crystal, but in such small amounts that they are too dilute to be dangerous
Cooking and dissolving in water turn the sodium and chlorine into harmless forms before the salt is eaten by anyone
Sodium chloride is a mixture of the two elements, and mixing the two dangerous elements cancels out their reactivity

question: Why can fractional distillation separate the hydrocarbons in crude oil?
correct: They have different boiling points, so they condense at different heights in the column
before: They don't dissolve in each other
after: They have different densities, so the heavier ones sink to the bottom of the column first
They have different solubilities, so each one dissolves out at a different height in the column
They react with the hot column at different rates, so each forms a new product at its own height

question: In paper chromatography an unknown gives one spot with Rf 0.62 in solvent A, matching a known dye. In solvent B it gives two spots. What should you conclude?
correct: The unknown is a mixture of two substances that happen to have the same Rf in solvent A
before: The unknown is the known dye
The experiment in solvent B failed
after: The unknown is the known dye, and solvent B has broken it down into two new substances
The unknown is pure, since one spot in any single solvent proves a substance has only one component
The unknown is the known dye, because an Rf match in one solvent is enough to identify a substance

question: Mixing two colourless solutions forms a yellow solid. What has most likely happened?

after: A physical change in which one of the solutions froze solid

question: When ammonium nitrate dissolves in water the temperature falls sharply. Is this evidence of a chemical reaction?
correct: Not by itself: dissolving is usually classed as physical, and an energy change alone doesn't prove a new substance has formed
before: Yes, any temperature change proves a reaction
Yes, because ammonium nitrate is a compound
No, because temperature changes never happen in reactions
after: Yes: a sharp temperature fall can only come from bonds forming in a reaction, so a new substance must have been made
Yes: ammonium nitrate is a compound, so whenever it is mixed with water a chemical reaction must take place
No: reactions always give out heat, so a fall in temperature proves that only a physical change has happened
